record.original_question: For a term-rewriting system R and a term t, define Spec(t) as the complete partial order of finite and infinite reduction sequences starting at t, modulo the quasi-order under which one sequence is below another when every term in the first eventually reduces to some term in the second. What properties does this spectrum have for special classes of rewrite systems, especially orthogonal systems and non-erasing systems, and how do those properties change when spectra of orthogonal systems are quotiented by Levy-style permutation equivalence?

evidence.quote: Investigate the properties of spectri for special classes of rewrite systems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R be a term-rewriting system over a signature, and let t be a term. A reduction sequence from t is a finite or infinite chain t = t_0 → t_1 → t_2 → ⋯ of one-step R-reductions. On the set of all such reduction sequences starting at t define the quasi-order ≼ by σ ≼ τ iff for every term s appearing in σ there exists a term s' appearing in τ such that s reduces (in finitely many R-steps) to s'. Let Spec(t) denote the resulting partially ordered set after identifying sequences that are ≼-equivalent; equip Spec(t) with its natural directed-suprema structure so that it becomes a complete partial order ("the spectrum of t").

(a) Determine the order-theoretic and topological properties of Spec(t) for general R, and in particular for the following classes:
   (i) orthogonal term-rewriting systems (left-linear with no critical pairs);
   (ii) non-erasing term-rewriting systems (every rewrite rule whose left-hand side contains a variable x also contains x on its right-hand side).

(b) For orthogonal R, consider the quotient of Spec(t) by Lévy's permutation equivalence on reductions (two co-initial reductions are Lévy-equivalent when they perform the same set of residual redex steps in possibly different orders). Describe how the structural properties identified in (a)(i) transfer to, or change in, this quotient cpo.
artifact.status_search_result: No source located that resolves the question of characterizing spectra of reduction sequences (as cpo's under the "eventually reduces to" quasi-order) for orthogonal or non-erasing rewriting systems, nor for their quotients by Lévy permutation equivalence. The problem is listed among open questions on rewriting and there is no published solution evident from current literature.

status_evidence.snippet: Curated list of open problems in rewriting maintained by the RTA community.
status_evidence.claim: The community-maintained RTA open problem list contains open structural questions on orthogonal rewriting systems, with no resolution recorded for spectra of reduction sequences.

status_evidence.title: Four equivalent equivalences of reductions
status_evidence.snippet: Two co-initial reductions in a term rewriting system are equivalent if they perform the same steps in different orders; characterizations via permutation, standardisation, labelling and projection.
status_evidence.claim: Lévy permutation equivalence is well-studied for orthogonal systems but the cpo structure of reduction-sequence spectra is not characterized in this line of work.
